attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: The 'I doubt' part is hedged and is not scored. The firm part is conditional: if such a moment exists, it will not happen this decade. The antecedent and qualifier are both kept.

contract.note: The contract treats the doubt as unscored, keeps the antecedent, and uses his own 'this decade', ending 2029-12-31. It requires broad historical recognition, not an executive's label. That is fair.

evidence.note: ABC report of Altman's 'in the singularity' remark, before the forecast interval. It is an executive declaration and does not establish a recognised single event.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast whose antecedent (a single recognised Singularity moment) is unknown, and its deadline (end of 2029) has not passed. Altman's declaration is only promotional context. No conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule, so it is not scored now.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: The drafter correctly keeps 'so far as I know'. The claim reports the limits of Marcus's knowledge and is not a categorical statement about the public record.

contract.note: The contract drops the 'so far as I know' hedge and scores an unhedged universal negative about the public record. It also counts a passing 2023 explanation as 'actually defined what they mean' for 2025-26 claims. The result depends on readings the speaker did not supply, and the plain-reading rule does not apply to hedged language.

evidence.note: 2023 CNBC transcript: Musk links singularity to the advent of AGI and to unpredictability. This would undercut an unhedged claim, but it does not test Marcus's hedged statement about what he knew, or what Musk meant in later claims.

reviews.rationale: The statement is hedged ('so far as I know'), so it is a report of limited knowledge, not a firm claim about the record. The contract scores a stronger unhedged version, and whether a 2023 remark counts as defining what they mean is a matter of interpretation. Musk's remark is noted but cannot score the hedged claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'Will surely improve greatly' is a firm forecast with no deadline. The 'may take decades' parenthetical is hedged and not scored.

contract.note: The contract reads 'greatly' as substantial, validated practical gains over the July 2026 baseline, which is an ordinary reading. It correctly says slow progress cannot contradict a forecast with no deadline. Labelling the claim 'retrospective' is a minor slip; it is prospective.

evidence.note: Nature Neuroscience paper (Sept 2026) on simultaneous speech and gesture decoding. When the work was done relative to the post, a baseline comparison, and replication are not established, so it does not meet the early-resolution rule.

reviews.rationale: The firm forecast has no deadline. The only evidence is one study whose achievement date and gain over the July 2026 baseline are not established. The early-resolution rule for support is not met, and absence of progress cannot contradict it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: An observation that the singularity has not been reached. 'Under any definition' slightly hardens the rhetorical 'no matter how you slice it', and the term itself lacks a threshold.

contract.note: The contract reasonably finds no definition-independent test. The context mixes several meanings (control, abundance, capability), and choosing one would narrow his claim.

evidence.note: Semafor, May 2026: Hassabis says singularity means 'the era we're in'. This shows how much the term's meaning varies; it is not evidence that any threshold was reached.

reviews.rationale: 'Singularity' has no agreed threshold, and the statement deliberately spans every reading of it. No observable test can settle the claim as stated. The evidence only documents that people use the term differently.
